key_insight: Recalling one image can be framed as a control problem: a learned conditioning signal guides a frozen diffusion model toward that image. The supplied abstract describes memory developing from an abstract gist toward exact, verbatim reproduction.
problem_solved: How does a generative model form a memory of a single image, and how can that recall be steered without changing the model itself?
method: Keep the pretrained diffusion model frozen.
Learn a conditioning signal that steers generation toward one target image.
Track how generated outputs evolve during training, from approximate recall to exact reproduction.
impact: This perspective treats memorization as a process to study and control, rather than only a failure mode. It could help practitioners investigate the boundary between generalized image generation and exact recall.
visual_elements: Training timeline showing generated images progressing from gist to verbatim recall.
Control diagram: learned conditioning signal → frozen diffusion model → reconstructed image.
Side-by-side comparison of the target image, early recall, and final reproduction.
Lock icon on the diffusion model and an adjustable knob on the conditioning signal.
paper_title: From Gist to Verbatim: The Controllable Path of One Image Through a Diffusion Prior
paper_authors: Luca Saglietti, Luca Giammanco, Marc Mezard, Chiara Plizzari, Luca Biggio
